title.narrative: Improved capacities of regional and sub regional constituents to promote fundamental principles and rights at work in Africa

description.narrative:
Despite efforts, child labour, human trafficking, forced labour, and modern slavery remain significant issues in Africa, with 92 million children in child labour, mostly in agriculture. The international community has set SDG Target 8.7 to eradicate these practices by 2025 and Target 8.5 to achieve decent work for all by 2030. The ILO leads initiatives like the Equal Pay International Coalition (EPIC) and Alliance 8.7 to meet these goals. The African Regional Academy on Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work, in collaboration with ITC in Turin, addresses socio-economic challenges in Africa. Additionally, the ILO collaborates with ACERWC, UNICEF, IOM, and AUC to support and protect vulnerable children, ensuring access to education and healthcare.
In February 2020, African Heads of State adopted the Ten-Year Action Plan to Eradicate Child Labour, Forced Labour, Human Trafficking, and Modern Slavery (2020-2030). This plan mobilizes African Union institutions, Member States, Regional Economic Commissions (RECs), and other partners to achieve AU Agenda 2063 and SDG Target 8.7. The plan emphasizes creating multi-stakeholder platforms for collaboration and knowledge sharing, and highlights the need for capacity building in child labour prevention and Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) standards.
